API Reference¶

ROTE separates its lightweight seed and metric API from optional neural evaluation and plotting. Importing rote_benchmark does not import PyTorch. The examples below use the public Python API; paper reproduction uses the command-line interface described in Experiments and Reproducibility.

Seed generation¶

LZW-controlled symbolic seeds for the ROTE benchmark.

rote_benchmark.generation.lzw_complexity(sequence)[source]¶

Count LZW output codes with the 52 ASCII letters as initial dictionary.

Parameters:

sequence (str)

Return type:

int

rote_benchmark.generation.lzw_string_generator(nr_symbols, target_complexity, priorise_complexity=True, random_state=42)[source]¶

Generate one symbolic seed at a requested LZW code count.

The random stream matches the historical generator while avoiding changes to the process-wide NumPy random state. priorise_complexity is retained for compatibility with the experimental protocol.

Parameters:

  • nr_symbols (int)

  • target_complexity (int)

  • priorise_complexity (bool)

  • random_state (int)

Return type:

tuple[str, int]

rote_benchmark.generation.lzw_string_seeds(symbols=(2, 4, 6, 8), complexity=(10, 30, 50, 70, 90), iterations=1, random_state=42, priorise_complexity=True)[source]¶

Return controlled seeds with the columns used by the ROTE experiments.

Seeds use random_state + index in the historical iteration order. Impossible alphabet/complexity pairs are skipped.

Parameters:

  • iterations (int)

  • random_state (int)

  • priorise_complexity (bool)

Return type:

DataFrame

The output of lzw_string_seeds is a DataFrame with nr_symbols, LZW_complexity, length, and string columns. A requested code count is a target; use the returned measured count in analyses.

Rollout distances¶

The two rollout distances reported by ROTE.

rote_benchmark.metrics.normalized_damerau_levenshtein_distance(source, target)[source]¶

Optimal-string-alignment edit distance divided by the longer length.

Parameters:

  • source (str)

  • target (str)

Return type:

float

rote_benchmark.metrics.normalized_jaro_winkler_distance(source, target, p=0.1)[source]¶

One minus Jaro-Winkler similarity, matching the manuscript runs.

Parameters:

  • source (str)

  • target (str)

  • p (float)

Return type:

float

Custom neural evaluation¶

Install .[neural] first. Import these names from rote_benchmark.evaluation. The complete model contract and runnable code are in Evaluating Your Own Model.

class rote_benchmark.metrics.EvaluationConfig(sequence_length=320, window_size=12, forecast_horizon=24, batch_size=32, max_epochs=12, patience=4, stopping_loss=0.05, optimizer='AdamW', learning_rate=0.001, weight_decay=0.0, lr_step_size=100, lr_gamma=0.5, device='cpu', seed=3407)¶

Immutable dataclass of training, split and rollout settings. A sequence must have room for the context, withheld suffix and chronological splits. optimizer is "Adam" or "AdamW". The default device is CPU.

rote_benchmark.metrics.evaluate_model(model, seed_string, *, config=None, name=None, run=0)¶

Train one prebuilt nn.Module or a fresh factory(n_symbols) and evaluate teacher-forced test windows plus closed-loop rollout. Returns a CSV-ready dict. A prebuilt module is fitted in place. The factory is called after setting config.seed. Raises ValueError for invalid model output shape or nonfinite logits.

rote_benchmark.metrics.score_model(model, seed_string, *, config=None, name=None)¶

Score a fitted nn.Module with no optimization. Returns a CSV-ready dict with test metrics, target and forecast strings, rollout distances and parameter count; no train-time or epoch fields are reported. The module is moved to config.device and left in eval mode. Use this for a checkpoint whose alphabet order and window size match the ROTE sequence.

rote_benchmark.metrics.evaluate_models(models, seed_string, *, config=None, runs=1)¶

Evaluate a mapping of model names to fresh factories using a shared seed and settings. Returns one pandas DataFrame row per model/run pair. The random seed for run \(r\) is config.seed + r.

Saved benchmark runs¶

rote_benchmark.artifacts uses pandas and the lightweight core only. run_benchmark additionally requires PyTorch and is imported from rote_benchmark.evaluation.

rote_benchmark.metrics.run_benchmark(models, seed_string, *, config=None, runs=1, output_dir=None, metadata=None)¶

Evaluate fresh model factories under one protocol, writing each completed record immediately. The second argument is one seed string or a mapping from seed ID to string for a complexity sweep. Return a SavedRun. output_dir=None creates a unique path beneath ./rote_runs or ROTE_RUNS_DIR; an explicit directory must not exist. metadata is a JSON-serializable mapping.

rote_benchmark.metrics.save_benchmark(results, config, *, output_dir=None)¶

Save an existing DataFrame and configuration mapping or dataclass in a new run directory. Return a SavedRun.

rote_benchmark.metrics.load_run(path)¶

Reload a run directory. Prefer the append-only JSONL records if present, so completed records survive interruption before CSV replacement.

class rote_benchmark.metrics.SavedRun(path, config, results, manifest)¶

Immutable container for the run directory, configuration dict, result DataFrame and progress manifest. Properties results_csv, records_jsonl, and events_jsonl give artifact paths.

Custom-model figures¶

Install .[plot] and import from rote_benchmark.visualization. All plot functions accept a result DataFrame, return a Matplotlib Figure, and optionally save an output path. The high-level function accepts a SavedRun, run directory, CSV path, or DataFrame.

class rote_benchmark.metrics.PlotStyle¶

Frozen dataclass controlling typography, colors, markers, line styles, figure size, uncertainty summaries, selected metrics, and file formats. See Results and Visualization for settings and a complete example.

rote_benchmark.metrics.visualize_benchmark(source, *, output_dir=None, style=None, figures=None, overwrite=False)¶

Save a coordinated report and visualization.json. Available figure names are quality, rollout, tradeoffs, and complexity. Existing files are protected unless overwrite=True. Returns a VisualizationReport with .path, .figures, and .config_path.

rote_benchmark.metrics.plot_model_comparison(results, output=None, *, style=None)¶

Point-and-error panels for configured teacher-forced and rollout metrics.

rote_benchmark.metrics.plot_rollout_error(results, output=None, *, style=None)¶

Prefix DL over horizon, with model styles and uncertainty bands.

rote_benchmark.metrics.plot_tradeoffs(results, output=None, *, style=None)¶

Rollout distance against available compute and resource measurements.

rote_benchmark.metrics.plot_complexity_sweep(results, output=None, *, style=None)¶

Mean metrics and variation against measured LZW code count; requires at least two distinct complexities.

Experiment commands¶

rote-bench
rote-matched-size
rote-plot
rote-plot-matched

rote-benchmark remains a compatibility alias for rote-bench. Use --help on each command for all options. The fixed-budget and matched-size CLI runners preserve the manuscript protocol and archived CSV schema. Their implementations live in rote_benchmark.benchmark and rote_benchmark.matched_size; specialized publication plots live in rote_benchmark.plotting and rote_benchmark.plot_matched. The generic custom-model plots are separate and do not alter publication figures.
